decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up right-arm approach toward the key; keep left arm parked. Adjust target to current key location and yaw.

Correct shaft centering from wrist feedback and begin closing around the narrow shaft near the bow.
Close fully, allow the grasp to settle, then begin a small vertical lift to check visual retention.
Key appears retained between the right fingers. Lift clear of the table, then begin rotating toward a central handover pose.
Carry the visibly retained key upward and inward while rotating it to present the bow toward the left hand.
Continue turning the right-held key toward the handover pose. Start the left arm's elbow-up approach with the gripper open.

Rotate the left gripper into a side-on receiving orientation while approaching the exposed key bow. Right hand remains closed and stationary.
Complete the left hand's side-on receiving orientation, stopping short of the bow. Keep right retention while checking the receiving alignment.
The key has tilted within the right grasp. Bring the left receiving fingers slightly lower and forward toward the visible bow, without releasing the right hand.
Track the tilted bow in the left wrist view and center it between the receiving fingers, maintaining right-hand retention.
The bow is now near the left finger center. Advance a few millimeters and close the receiver fully while the right hand still supports the key.
Keep the left receiver fully closed and gradually release the right grasp to verify that the bow is retained by the left fingers.

Recover the settled key with the right hand. Rotate the open gripper to its new shaft direction while descending cautiously; left hand stays clear.
Continue rotating the right gripper toward the recovered key's shaft and descending, with both arms remaining in their own workspaces.
Align the open fingers with the key now resting on edge. Continue a slow vertical approach while watching the bow and shaft.
Finish aligning along the shaft and approach its base above the table. The key is on its edge, so stop slightly higher before closing.
Retract the left hand to provide more clearance. Center the right grasp at the shaft base and close gradually on the edge-on key.
Hold the left arm at its last accepted configuration. Close the centered right grasp fully, settle, and test retention with a small lift.
The edge-on key appears retained. Lift it clear while slowly orienting its bow toward the left hand for a deeper, more secure transfer.
The key slipped and is now flat on the table. Reopen and approach the shaft base for a lower, deeper pinch rather than lifting the edge-on grasp.
Refine the new flat-key approach from the wrist image: move toward the shaft, straighten the finger alignment, and lower in small increments.
Recenter the shaft after its slight table motion. Adjust yaw and lateral position at nearly constant clearance before closing.
The key is being nudged during low lateral motion. Lift the open right fingers clear before recentering, then approach vertically.
At clear height, align the right wrist above the settled key shaft and rotate to match its new diagonal orientation before descending.
Raise farther to guarantee clearance from the key before any further lateral or yaw correction.
Use the now-clear overhead view to align above the shaft near its bow. Rotate toward the settled diagonal key direction without touching the table.
Continue matching the shaft direction while bringing the open gripper closer from above; monitor the key for any unwanted table motion.
Center the visible bow and shaft under the right gripper, finish the small yaw correction, and descend toward a vertical pinch.
Use wrist-image alignment to bring the shaft base down into the finger-pad region and center its lateral offset; keep the receiver stationary.
Stop yawing and lower toward the visible shaft base, making only a small image-centering correction before partially closing.
Close on the shaft now positioned in the finger-pad region, lower only a few millimeters for purchase, and test a small lift.
Check whether the newly closed grasp actually retains the key with a slow, short vertical lift; avoid further rotation until retention is visible.
The key remains on the table. Reopen and reposition toward the bow so the narrow shaft, rather than its tip, lies between the finger pads.
Align the flat key's shaft under the right finger center and descend to grasp height, keeping the fingers open until centered.
Stop rotating. Center the bow within the open fingers, lower slightly, and close fully for a broader purchase on the key.
Allow the right fingers to finish closing without lateral motion, then test only a few millimeters of lift for bow retention.

Continue the retained-key rotation and lift toward the receiving pose; keep both arms separated and the left fingers open.

Keep the receiving hand still and continue the right-hand yaw and lift, maintaining a fully closed grasp.
